claim: k3d v5.9.0 linux-arm64, Helm v3.22.1 and Fleet v0.16.3 (fleet-crd, fleet, fleet-agent charts and the fleet CLI) matched their pins and upstream checksum files; the pulled rancher/k3s:v1.37.2-k3s1 digest equals the os/versions.lock.yaml pin (sha256:21ea6e0f…); Fleet images rancher/fleet@sha256:a1696682faa6… and rancher/fleet-agent@sha256:a657a2a3a93a…

Three k3s clusters (box-1, site-b, two-node site-a) registered with one ClusterRegistrationToken by agent-initiated registration and were Ready 63 s after the agent installs; a DOCKER-USER rule dropping every new connection from the hub container to any site container counted 0 packets while a counter on site-to-hub API connections counted 9
The first release (ConfigMap + Deployment of the k3s pause image) reached all three clusters and was Available in 18 s

With manual partitions ring0/ring1/ring2, maxUnavailable: 0 and maxUnavailablePartitions: 0, a new (bad) release never reached ring 0 in 15 minutes: all three BundleDeployments kept the old deployment ID while the bundle reported WaitApplied on every partition (pre-registered T3 FAIL)

In the same run a later good release (v3) got a staged deployment ID on the ring-0 cluster that was never promoted; Fleet showed that cluster as OutOfSync (1/2 bundles ready); run 1 was stopped after T3
Exploratory E5 (maxUnavailable: 0, maxUnavailablePartitions: 1): no cluster received the new release in about 2.5 minutes before the variant was stopped; the bundle counted two partitions unavailable

Footprint in this lab: Fleet manager pods on the hub about 170 MiB working set in total (controller 30, agent-management 34, gitjob 22, helmops 16, cleanup 24, local agent 44 MiB); the Fleet agent on each downstream cluster 42-49 MiB; k3s node containers about 0.6 GB (sites) and 0.95 GB (hub)

Exploratory E6 (maxUnavailable: 1, maxUnavailablePartitions: 0): a bad release reached ring 0 (box-1) in 17 s and was held there for the 6-minute window (site-b and site-a stayed on v1; bundle: ring 0 NotReady 'Progress deadline exceeded', other rings WaitApplied); re-applying v1 restored box-1 in 17 s; a good release then reached all three clusters within one 16 s poll (ring order not resolvable at that resolution)

Exploratory E6, partition: with site-b (ring 1) stopped, a new release reached box-1 (ring 0) but site-a (ring 2) did not receive it during the 5-minute outage (Fleet reported site-a and site-b not ready); 48 s after site-b was started again, all three clusters had the release and were Available

Exploratory E3: a ConfigMap deleted by hand on a downstream cluster was not restored by Fleet within 300 s, and the hub still reported that cluster with 2/2 bundles ready (default settings, drift correction not enabled)
